title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes Grothendieck works with 'mégaris'. A mégaris is a set M of abstract 'figures' carrying three relations: ≤ (face/boundary incidence), ≪̊ (interior inclusion) and |o| (disjointness of interiors). These are subject to axioms Mag 1–4. The 'lieux' (points) are recovered as minimal elements. On pp. 81–83 he builds the mégaris attached to an ordered set L. The figures are points P_x = {{x}} and segments S_{a,b} = {[a,b], {a}, {b}} for a<b. The boundary is ∂S_{a,b} = {P_a, P_b}, and ∂P_x = ∅.

This page has three parts.

(A3) It completes the totally ordered, divisible case (]a,b[ ≠ ∅ whenever a<b) by making |o| explicit:
- P_x |o| P_y iff x ≠ y, i.e. x<y or y<x.
- P_x |o| S_{a,b} iff x ≤ a or b ≤ x.
- S_{a,b} |o| S_{a',b'} iff a<b≤a'<b' or a'<b'≤a<b.
He remarks that this just expresses |X|° ∩ |Y|° = ∅, with |P_x|° = {x} and |S_{a,b}|° = ]a,b[, and that divisibility is used. A partly illegible paragraph says that, in the present set-theoretic setting, more axioms come for free. The reason is the existence of a faithful 'support' function X ↦ |X| (not necessarily commuting with unions), or alternatively X ↦ Ouv X.

(B) For an arbitrary poset L he keeps the same M = M_0 ⊔ M_1 inside P(P(L)). A margin note says one could more simply take M_0 = L and M_1 = {(a,b) : a<b}. But the S_{a,b} need no longer be genuine elementary figures, because ]a,b[ may be empty (covering pairs). So he defines ≤, ≪̊ and |o| by the explicit order-theoretic formulas rather than by set-theoretic ones. He warns that S_{a,b} ≪̊ S_{a',b'} ⇔ a' ≤ a < b ≤ b' implies ]a,b[ ⊂ ]a',b'[, but not conversely.

Margin NB: in this adaptation one gets 'pseudo-figures' (non-empty, with empty interior). The relations ≤ and ≪ can still be read set-theoretically, but |o| cannot, except in the totally ordered case. The reason is that P_x |o| P_y is defined as comparability: two incomparable points are distinct but not 'disjoint'. The next page checks Mag 1–4. It notes that the minimal elements for ≪̊ also include the S_{a,b} with ]a,b[ = ∅. The lieux remain identified with L.

Purpose: to supply a basic test example (a one-dimensional 'interval mégaris') for the axiomatics of a point-free, combinatorial analysis situs. The example shows how points are recovered as minimal elements, and how interior and disjointness relations behave when the underlying order is not dense or not total.
errors: Totally ordered case is correct. If a'<b and a<b', then ]a,b[ ∩ ]a',b'[ = ]max(a,a'), min(b,b')[, which is non-empty by divisibility. So disjointness of interiors is exactly b ≤ a' or b' ≤ a, as stated.

The ⇏ written over ⟺ in '|S_{a,b}|* ⊂ |S_{a',b'}|*' is unclear. If |·| means the support [a,b], then [a,b] ⊂ [a',b'] does imply a' ≤ a and b ≤ b', so the equivalence holds. The next page indeed states X ≪ Y ⟺ |X| ⊂ |Y|. The failure only concerns interiors (]a,b[ may be empty), which is what the corrected line with ° says.

In the general poset case the definition P_x |o| P_y ⟺ x, y comparable deliberately departs from 'disjoint interiors' ({x} ∩ {y} = ∅ for all x ≠ y). This is a choice rather than an error, acknowledged in the margin and on the next page.
Next page (not this one) has a slip, 'y ≥ b' for 'x ≥ b'.

ideas.what: Mégaris attached to a (totally ordered, divisible) set: points P_x and segments S_{a,b}, with face, interior-inclusion and interior-disjointness relations written explicitly; points recovered as minimal elements
ideas.modern_name: 1-dimensional cell/interval structure on an ordered set; close to mereotopological (point-free) models of the line
ideas.usually_credited_to: Point-free geometry: Whitehead, de Laguna (1920s), Tarski; mereotopology: Clarke (1981) and later
ideas.where_published: Unpublished 'Analysis situs' manuscripts (1986); the general programme of tame topology is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme, but not this formalism

ideas.what: Using divisibility (density) of a total order to identify combinatorial disjointness with set-theoretic disjointness of open intervals
ideas.modern_name: density of linear orders / order topology

ideas.what: Extension to arbitrary posets producing 'pseudo-figures' (segments with empty interior at covering pairs), with disjointness of points defined as comparability rather than distinctness
ideas.modern_name: comparability graph / 1-skeleton of the order complex; comparability as an 'apartness' relation
ideas.usually_credited_to: order complex: classical (Alexandrov/Dowker era); apartness: Brouwer/Heyting

ideas.what: Remark that a faithful support functor X ↦ |X| (or X ↦ Ouv X) to subsets lets one transport axioms from set theory, so fewer axioms need direct checking
ideas.modern_name: faithful realization/representation of an abstract incidence structure in a power set

missed.claim: The mégaris axiomatics shares the core moves of mereotopology and point-free geometry. These are a primitive part relation, interior parthood and disjointness, with points recovered as minimal elements ('lieux'). It is an independent reinvention of a Whitehead/Clarke-type theory with a combinatorial-topological aim. To my knowledge this link is not discussed in the literature on Grothendieck's late manuscripts.
missed.quote: Ici encore, les P_x sont les minimaux à la fois pour ≤ et pour ≪̊ ... ensemble des lieux s'identifie à L (next page); |S_{a,b}|° = [a,b]∖{a,b} = ]a,b[
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Puts Grothendieck's unpublished 'analysis situs' in dialogue with formal mereotopology (region connection calculus, contact algebras). This is mainly of historical and philosophical interest.

missed.claim: He observes that for non-total posets |o| is no longer the set-theoretic disjointness of interiors: incomparable distinct points are not 'disjoint'. He does not say which notion of separation is intended or why comparability is the right choice (presumably to satisfy Mag 3/Mag 4).
missed.quote: Mais pas |o|, sauf dans le cas tot. ordonné.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It marks where the axioms force a non-set-theoretic disjointness, a possible test case for the robustness of the mégaris axioms.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine worked example (points and intervals of an ordered set) inside an unpublished axiomatics. The mathematics is elementary and correct. The only mild interest is the point-free/mereotopological flavour of the whole project and the observation about non-total orders.
transcription_corrections: Top of the brace: the small annotation reads 'de L' (or '∂L'), attached to the comparison x<y in L.
Second case: 'x ≤ a ou b ≤ x' (the ≤ before x is overwritten, b ⋦ x / b ≤ x).

The paragraph 'Dans le contexte ensembliste actuel...' is largely illegible. Words like 'grosse' and 'commutant pas tous unions' are guesses; the clear content is 'grâce à l'existence de la fonction support fidèle X ↦ |X|' and 'on prend cette fois la fonction support fidèle X ↦ Ouv X'.

Margin NB more plausibly reads: 'NB Avec la présente adaptation, on trouve des pseudo-figures élémentaires dans L (non vides, avec |X|° = ∅) (on peut [définir] ≪̊ ... réduit à ≤ ...) [via] les relations ensemblistes. Mais pas |o|, sauf dans le cas tot. ordonné.'

The symbol over the double arrow in 'a' ≤ a < b ≤ b' ⟺ |S_{a,b}|* ⊂ |S_{a',b'}|*' is a struck-through implication (⇏). A crossed-out line beneath it begins 'by ...'; the next line, with °, is the retained version.
